newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.C. Water Authority sets $220 mln bond sale.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.C. Water Authority sets $220 mln bond sale.

text.p: New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority plans to sell $220 million of new money bonds Oct 16, a city official said Friday, adding that PaineWebber Inc will run the books.
"There may be a variable component in addition to the fixed rate," said the city official, explaining the final details still are being worked out. He spoke on condition of anonymity.

On October 2, New York City expects to sell through competition a total of about $1.6 billion of Revenue Anticipation Notes. Around $550 million of these notes will mature in April, while another $1.050 billion of the offering will mature on June 30.
The bigger section of the note sale will be backed by a letter of credit from three banks, the Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, the Bank of Nova Scotia, and the Commerce Bank CBVA.O.
Further, the city is expected to sell general obligation bonds through its syndicate by negotiation at the end of October.
While the city official declined to comment on the bond sale, city sources have speculated the offering might include as much of $500 million of new money bonds.
And the city might elect to sell $250 million to $500 million of refunding bonds at the same time, they said.
